Job Description: 
 Respiratory Protection Regulatory Engagement Specialist 
 Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World 
 Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.
 This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military experience to a 3M career. 
 As a Respiratory Protection Regulatory Engagement Specialist in 3M’s Personal Safety Division (PSD), you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world.
 You will collaborate with multidisciplinary colleagues around the world to advance respiratory protection standards, regulations, and occupational health and safety (OHS) practices across global markets. You will represent 3M in high-impact regulatory and standards-development activities, engaging with OHS professionals, industry stakeholders, and regulators as a technical thought leader. In this role, you will shape science-based approaches and provide technical leadership.
 Here, you will make an impact by:
 Facilitating the development of science-based performance and selection and use standards for respiratory protection equipment and occupational health and safety, while tracking progress and key milestones.
 Identifying opportunities to advance respirator related health and safety policies and regulations and developing strategies to implement science-based approaches.
 Helping to coach, mentor, develop, and coordinate PSD’s global team of application engineers and regulatory specialists engaged in respiratory protection standards development activities.
 Collaborating with professional associations, educational organizations, public health organizations, and relevant government entities.
 Representing 3M in standards development organizations and related technical committees.
 Collaborating with cross-functional teams to align on PSD’s highest-priority respirator related standards and regulations that support business growth.
 Leading respirator related research to support new technologies and existing products.
 Communicating emerging respiratory protection standards, regulatory, and policy developments to relevant stakeholders and translating their potential implications into actionable business guidance.
 Your Skills and Expertise 
 To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M is looking for candidates who must have the following qualifications:  
 Bachelor’s degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start)
 Five (5) years of experience with respiratory protection-related occupational health and safety regulations and performance standards in a private, public, government or military environment.
 Master’s degree in occupational health and safety, industrial hygiene, public policy, regulatory affairs, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
 Experience representing an organization with regulatory agencies, standards-development organizations, industry associations, policymakers, or government affairs stakeholders.
 Experience conducting or leading applied research in respiratory protection or personal protective equipment.
 Ability to translate complex technical, regulatory, or policy information into clear guidance for diverse audiences.
 Strong communication, influencing, stakeholder-management, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
 Ability to work effectively across cultures, geographies, and global teams.
 Work location: 
 This role follows an on-site working model, requiring the employee to work at least four days a week at the 3M Center in Maplewood, MN or London, Ontario.
 Travel: May include up to 25% domestic and international 
 Relocation Assistance: Is not authorized 
 Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status). 
 Supporting Your Well-being 
 3M offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, 3M regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope.
 Chat with Max 
 For assistance with searching through our current job openings or for more information about all things 3M, visit Max, our virtual recruiting assistant on 3M.com/careers.

This range represents a good faith estimate for this position. The specific compensation offered to a candidate may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s relevant knowledge, training, skills, work location, and/or experience. In addition, this position may be eligible for a range of benefits (e.g., Medical, Dental & Vision, Health Savings Accounts, Health Care & Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, Disability Benefits, Life Insurance, Voluntary Benefits, Paid Absences and Retirement Benefits, etc.). Additional information is available at: https://www.3m.com/3M/en_US/careers-us/working-at-3m/benefits/. 
Good Faith Posting Date Range 10/27/2026 To 11/26/2026 Or until filled

This agreement lays out key terms on using 3M Confidential Information and Trade Secrets. It also has provisions discussing conflicts of interest and how inventions are assigned.  - Build scalable and reusable tools for digging into model performance.

Qualifications:

 - You enjoy rapidly building prototypes that demonstrate the boundaries of what LLMs are capable of, and you have developed resources to measure those capabilities.

 - You have spent dozens of hours reviewing complex data and LLM outputs to ensure high data quality.

Department: COVID Genomics  
 The Role: 
To provide technical support for real-time PCR testing within the Virology department and to support the overall Covid response within laboratory operations manual set up of real time PCR to the molecular laboratory and to support laboratory operations for Covid PCR. 
 Key Responsibilities- 
 Under the guidance of a Medical Laboratory Technologist or Molecular Specialist, manual or partially-automated set up of real-time PCR, including preparation of primer and probe stocks, and Sanger sequencing.
 Manual or automated extraction of nucleic acids on high throughput platforms as assigned.
 Operation of real-time thermalcycler, extraction platforms, Sanger sequencing platform, and automated liquid handling platforms.
 Real-time PCR data analysis using vendor thermalcycling software.
 Technical support for validation or evaluation studies under the direction of the manager, team lead, MLT or molecular specialist.
 Handling or processing of human specimens including respiratory specimens, blood, urine is advantageous.
 Prioritizes work and responds to urgent or unpredictable demands.
 Other duties as assigned.
 Knowledge and Skills- 
 Strong understanding molecular theory and best practices including real-time PCR, nucleic acid extraction, molecular workflows, primer and probe dilution calculation and preparation is a strong asset.
 Experience with standard molecular lab applications and instrumentation (e.g. DNA extraction, pipetting, PCR set up, sequencing) an asset.
 Familiarity with general laboratory equipment including centrifuges, incubators, pipettors, automated liquid handlers, incubators, biological safety cabinets.
 Good working understanding of and experience using Microsoft Word, Excel, Access.
 Time management and ability to prioritize.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 High degree of comfort with automation.
 Adaptability to changing demands and willingness to learn.
 Understanding of Sanger sequencing and Next Generation Sequencing theory is an asset.
 Education and Experience- 
 Bachelor of Science.
 Minimum of 6 months of real-time PCR, preferably in a clinical genetics or molecular genetics laboratory.
 Attributes and Competencies- 
 Works within established procedures for a Medical Laboratory Assistant and within PHO Lab standards and protocols.
 Follows technical instructions (SOP) for testing of samples and preparation of reagents.
 Solves basic problems (e.g., mismatched samples, issues with prepared media such as incorrect pH).
 Seeks advice and direction in solving more complex problems.
 Determines which organisms can/cannot be handled due to safety/risk.
 May be required to lift up to 10 kg..
 May be required to work within a biological safety cabinet/fumehood.
 Physical coordination and manual dexterity in the use of keyboard, operate and maintain laboratory equipment, and perform testing of specimens.
 May be required to perform repetitive tasks such as pipetting.
 May be required to stand or sit for the period of one shift.
 Requires physical activity such as walking, lifting, stretching and bending.
 May be required to work shifts as scheduled.
 Works within a Laboratory environment which contains hazardous and infectious materials, odors, noise generated from automated analyzers, some temperature extremes, such as walk in fridges and freezers.
 Required to adhere to Laboratory safety including proper use of biological safety cabinets, autoclaves and personal protective equipment.
 Works shifts as assigned.

Nous ne pratiquons aucune discrimination fondée sur la race, la religion, la couleur, l'origine nationale, le sexe, l'orientation sexuelle, l'âge, l'état civil, le handicap ou le statut de vétéran. Des aménagements pour les candidats handicapés sont disponibles sur demande à toutes les étapes du processus de recrutement. 
 À propos de Broccolini 
 Broccolini est une entreprise familiale intégrée offrant des services en construction, développement et immobilier à travers le Canada, dans les secteurs industriel, commercial et résidentiel. Nous sommes reconnus pour la qualité de notre travail, notre collaboration ouverte et nos standards élevés — et nous appliquons cette même approche à la façon dont nous bâtissons nos équipes et notre culture.
 À propos du rôle 
 Le directeur ou la directrice, Préconstruction est responsable du processus de soumission de bout en bout : de l'évaluation initiale des opportunités d'affaires et de la décision de participer ou non, jusqu'à la soumission finale et au transfert vers l'équipe de construction. Ce rôle ne se substitue pas aux responsables de discipline qui gèrent l'estimation, la planification, les affaires juridiques ou la SST : il les coordonne. Le mandat consiste à apporter une stratégie de soumission unifiée, une propriété claire des livrables et une exécution intégrée à chaque appel d'offres significatif.
 Il s'agit d'un rôle transversal offrant une visibilité sur l'ensemble du portefeuille Broccolini. La personne retenue travaillera directement avec la haute direction et devra faire preuve d'un haut degré d'autonomie, d'influence sans autorité hiérarchique, et d'une imputabilité orientée vers les résultats.
 Responsabilité  
 Pilotage des soumissions 
 Piloter les décisions de participation ou non aux appels d'offres, en appliquant des critères d'évaluation structurés et en validant la capacité organisationnelle disponible.
 Élaborer la stratégie de soumission pour chaque appel d'offres : profil de risque, hypothèses clés et attribution des responsabilités par discipline
 Présenter les recommandations de participation et les stratégies de soumission à la haute direction
 S'assurer que chaque soumission est dotée des ressources nécessaires et correctement séquencée pour respecter les échéances sans compromettre la qualité
 Coordination interfonctionnelle 
 Coordonner les responsables de discipline (estimation, planification, affaires juridiques, SST, propositions) en vue d'une soumission intégrée et cohérente
 Gérer la mobilisation des consultants externes et des experts internes tout au long de la phase de préconstruction
 Assurer la gouvernance des livrables : maintenir le plan directeur, suivre les engagements, identifier les écarts et escalader rapidement
 Faciliter l'alignement entre les fonctions lorsque la portée, les risques ou les exigences du client évoluent en cours de soumission
 Processus et amélioration continue 
 Assurer la propriété et l'amélioration continue du processus de préconstruction : gabarits, rythmes de travail, listes de vérification et protocoles de transfert
 Réaliser des rétrospectives après les gains, les pertes et à la clôture des projets, et alimenter les standards avec les leçons apprises
 Maintenir une vue consolidée de toutes les soumissions actives et en rendre compte régulièrement à la haute direction
 Leadership et gestion des personnes 
 Constituer, diriger et développer l'équipe de préconstruction
 Définir des attentes de performance claires, accompagner le développement des membres de l'équipe et traiter directement les lacunes
 Cultiver une culture d'imputabilité, de collaboration et d'amélioration continue
 Ce que nous recherchons 
 Expérience 
 10 ans et plus d'expérience en construction ou en développement immobilier intégré, avec une exposition significative à la préconstruction
 Expérience avérée dans la direction de processus de soumission complexes et multidisciplinaires, de l'identification de l'occasion jusqu'à la remise du dossier
 Une expérience dans plusieurs secteurs constitue un atout
 Expérience dans la présentation de recommandations et l'animation de discussions à l'échelon de la haute direction
 Leadership et compétences 
 Pensée stratégique permettant de développer une approche de soumission gagnante, et pas seulement de gérer un processus
 Leadership interfonctionnel solide : capacité à aligner les pairs et à les tenir imputables sans autorité hiérarchique directe
 Grande rigueur organisationnelle, avec un historique de mise en place de systèmes de gouvernance qui perdurent
 Communication claire et directe en français et en anglais (bilinguisme fortement souhaité)

The Role 
 BeyondTrust is seeking a Senior Staff Software Development Engineer to set the technical direction for NHI Governance. NHI Governance is the Pathfinder Insights module that discovers, assesses, and remediates non-human identities — service principals, IAM users, access keys and secrets, workload identities, and AI agents — across Microsoft Entra ID, AWS, and on-premise environments. The system spans .NET 10 services over PostgreSQL; an inventory pipeline fed from governed Databricks lakehouse views; durable Temporal workflows (Python workers, a .NET gateway, protobuf contracts) that onboard, rotate, reduce access for, and decommission live customer credentials, with custody in BeyondTrust Password Safe and storage adapters for AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, and HashiCorp Vault; and Angular micro-frontends in the Insights console. It ships through GitOps to Amazon EKS in commercial and government environments.
 As one of the most senior engineers on the team, you will own the architecture across these pieces and the contracts that hold them together, lead the system from prototype to hardened production, and act as a force multiplier for a team that works in an AI-assisted, agent-native way.
 What You’ll Do 
 Own end-to-end architecture for NHI Governance across its services, the workflow layer it shares with the platform team, and the data lineage from the Insights lakehouse — and decide where each boundary lives.
 Design the source and vault plug-in seams (today Entra and AWS are bespoke), so a new identity source or vault becomes a repeatable, conformance-tested addition rather than a rewrite.
 Define and evolve the contracts other teams build on: service APIs and protobuf workflow schemas with breaking-change gates.
 Set the safety model for credential-lifecycle automation — rotation, decommissioning, access reduction, approvals, compensation, and points of no return — where a defect can revoke a customer's production credential.
 Define the least-privilege permission model customers grant us in Entra ID, AWS, and Password Safe, feature by feature. Own how it is verified live and explained in the product, and the setup assets (scripts, templates) that grant exactly that and no more.
 Lead the path from prototype to production: service-to-service authentication, tenant isolation, FIPS-compliant builds, and promotion through commercial and government environments.
 Design how our own services obtain identities and secrets across AWS accounts, regions, and environments — least privilege, workload identity, no long-lived keys.
 Partner with product, platform, data, and security leaders to align technical strategy with the roadmap; make the build/buy and architectural trade-off calls.
 Raise how the team builds: design reviews, testing against real dependencies and live test tenants, and the conventions and guardrails for AI-assisted development.

About Clutch: 
 Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, helping customers buy and sell cars from home. From browsing vehicles online to doorstep delivery and our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee, we’re making the experience simpler from start to finish.
 Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Toronto, we’re growing quickly and looking for curious, driven people who want to help shape how Canadians buy, sell, and own cars. Learn more at clutch.ca .
 About the role: 
 Every car Clutch buys and sells starts with a pricing decision. For sellers, it’s the offer they accept or walk away from. For buyers, it’s one of the first things they compare. We’re hiring a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to help build the framework behind those decisions, from what we pay for a vehicle to what we list it for and how its price changes over time.
 You’ll build models, turn predictions into pricing decisions, and design experiments to measure their impact. You’ll own your work through production, including the pipelines, monitoring, and evaluation that keep models reliable. Because pricing outcomes can take weeks to emerge, you’ll also develop faster signals to help us understand what’s working.
 You’ll sit on Clutch’s pricing team and partner closely with acquisition, retail operations, finance, product, and engineering. Your work will be visible, measurable, and directly tied to margins, inventory performance, and the customer experience.
 What you’ll do: 
 Build the models behind vehicle valuation, expected sale proceeds, and time to sale, owning feature engineering, model development, calibration, and retraining.
 Turn model predictions into pricing decisions that account for business constraints, using optimization methods and thoughtful problem formulation.
 Own evaluation, building offline metrics that reflect business outcomes and using holdouts and historical replays to distinguish real improvements from random variation.
 Take your models into production and keep them reliable, owning training pipelines, serving, consistency between training and serving features, monitoring, and drift detection.
 Design and analyze experiments to understand how pricing changes affect vehicle sales and business performance.
 Work with analysts and operations teams to turn their market knowledge into useful model inputs and investigate quickly when predictions don’t reflect reality.
 Quantify the impact of pricing improvements and turn your findings into clear recommendations on where to invest next.
 What we’re looking for: 
 Must Haves 
 Production ML experience: 6+ years in a hands-on machine learning role, with a track record of models that improved business outcomes. You’ve owned models from training through deployment and ongoing operation, including pipelines, versioning, monitoring, and tools such as MLflow.
 Breadth across modeling approaches: Experience with deep learning for regression and classification, recommender systems, statistical modeling, experiment design, and linear and nonlinear constrained optimization. You have depth in several areas and can build working competence in the others.
 Strong engineering fundamentals: Strong Python and SQL, along with experience building services, writing tests, and working with CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, and orchestration.
 Statistical rigor: You can design and analyze A/B tests, choose methods appropriate to the underlying distributions, and reason about identification, confounding, variance, sample size, and power.
 Business judgment: You know how to connect model performance to business results and identify which problems are worth solving.
 Clear communication: You can explain technical findings and trade-offs to nontechnical partners, make actionable recommendations, and hold a thoughtful point of view when challenged.
 Nice to Have 
 Experience with pricing, revenue management, or marketplace dynamics.
 Working knowledge of TypeScript, which is used in much of the application consuming these models.
 Experience with causal inference and quasi-experimental methods when randomization isn’t available.
 Analytics engineering experience, including warehouse models, data contracts, and testing.
 Experience with physical inventory where individual units are unique, depreciate, and carry holding costs, particularly automotive, wholesale auctions, or vehicle valuation.
 What success looks like: 
 In the first 3 months: You understand the pricing framework, its weaknesses, and their business impact. You’ve identified an opportunity, developed a hypothesis, and run an experiment to test it.
 By 6 months: You own one or more parts of the framework. Your work has delivered measurable business value, and you can demonstrate what drove the improvement.
 By 12 months: You’ve identified and built a missing capability. Your findings are changing how Clutch makes pricing decisions.
 Why you’ll love it at Clutch: 
 Ownership of meaningful problems, with room to shape your approach and see it through.
 Competitive pay and the opportunity to share in Clutch’s growth through stock options.
 Time off to rest and recharge.
 Health and dental coverage to support you and your family.
 Employment Type: 
 New, Permanent Full-Time.
 Hybrid, with three days per week at our downtown Toronto office.
 Compensation & Benefits: 
 Annual Base Salary: $180,000+ CAD.
 Equity: Stock options.
 Coverage: Healthcare, dental, vision, prescription drugs, life insurance, and coverage for eligible dependents.
 Compensation considers relevant skills, performance, market benchmarks, role responsibilities, and working conditions.
 Clutch welcomes people with different backgrounds and perspectives and is committed to an accessible hiring process. For accommodation at any interview stage, contact talent@clutch.ca.

We are building the future of AI-native performance marketing, and we need someone to own it.

 We're hiring a Performance Marketing Manager (AI & Growth): a hybrid growth practitioner who combines data-driven media buying with technical infrastructure skills and a real appetite for AI innovation.
 You will own our paid acquisition campaigns end to end, build and maintain the measurement stack that connects ad spend to HubSpot accounts and deals (GTM, server-side GTM, GA4, Conversions API), and shape our next generation of marketing execution by building AI agents, automated workflows and AI-assisted creative pipelines.

 Plan, launch and scale paid acquisition campaigns across Meta, Google Ads, LinkedIn and other platforms to hit strict CAC, LTV and ROAS targets.

 Continually test and optimize funnels to convert cold traffic into qualified CRM leads and customers.

 Set up and troubleshoot Conversions API (CAPI) integrations and server-to-server tracking to ensure resilient attribution.

 Push CRM stage changes back to the ad networks as offline conversions so the algorithms optimize on qualified accounts, not form fills.
 Growth Innovation, AI Agents and Creative Systems (20%) 
 Build and deploy AI agents and automated workflows that handle operational marketing loops (campaign reporting, lead enrichment, ad monitoring).
 Partner with our Lead Designer and Brand Marketing Manager to build scalable AI creative pipelines using the latest image, video and copy generation models, to rapidly iterate ad assets and lifecycle email campaigns.
 Pioneer new AI-driven marketing methods that multiply the output of our growth engine.

 Attribution you can trust: every paid lead is tied to its campaign and ad in HubSpot, with no double counting and no drop-offs between form, CRM and ad platforms.

 Startup or small-company experience where you built the stack and the playbook from scratch.

 As the Trade Compliance Officer for TCDS in Canada, you will lead the TCDS trade compliance team and oversee the operational aspects of the local trade compliance program that are implemented by other functions in TCDS and direct the trade compliance tasks related to Canadian export controls & licensing, export reporting, sanctions, and customs processes.  This role will also support the Thales Canada trade compliance team when needed to provide similar support to other BLs when required.
 Key Areas of Responsibility  
 Oversee, manage, and direct the trade compliance program for TCDS Canadian operations and ensuring alignment with Canadian, US and any other applicable export control, sanctions, and customs requirements.
